name: Costa Natura Naturist Resort
tagline: Spain's oldest beachfront naturist resort — Costa del Sol
location: Estepona, Costa del Sol (45 min from Málaga airport)
best_for: Naturists seeking beachfront access in a long-established community

contact.address: Ctra. de Cádiz km 151, Estepona, Province of Málaga, Spain

description: The oldest naturist resort in Spain — established in 1976 on a private stretch of Costa del Sol beach between Estepona and Marbella. With over 200 studios and apartments in traditional Andalusian style, a long private beach, pool with jacuzzi, and beachside restaurant, Costa Natura is the historic heart of Spanish naturism. Accommodation quality varies; renovated units offer a significant upgrade.
highlights: Private naturist beach directly on the Costa del Sol
Traditional Andalusian architecture in a lush garden setting
Pool with jacuzzi and beachside restaurant (Renato's)
6km from Estepona town; good restaurant selection nearby
considerations: Apartment quality varies significantly — request a renovated unit
Car or taxi required; limited public transport
Beach is darker sand/pebble, not fine white sand
Some areas showing age and need of maintenance

reviews.name: AndreaBH
reviews.text: Costa Natura is a gem on the Costa del Sol — beautifully situated right on the beach between Estepona and Marbella. The white Andalusian-style buildings, lush gardens, and beachside restaurant create a genuinely relaxing atmosphere. We stayed in one of the renovated beachfront apartments with stunning sea views. The restaurant serves excellent fresh fish. The beach itself is private and long enough to find your own space. A little remote without a car, but absolutely worth it for naturists.

reviews.name: ReturnVisitor12
reviews.text: We have been coming to Costa Natura for twelve years and it never disappoints. The naturist community here is welcoming, respectful, and wonderfully diverse. The gardens are beautifully maintained, the pool and jacuzzi always clean, and the beachside kiosk is perfect for a cold drink mid-afternoon. Yes, some apartments are more modern than others — request one that has been renovated — but overall this remains the finest naturist beachfront resort in Spain.

reviews.name: SteveM_UK
reviews.text: Having read mixed reviews I was pleasantly surprised. Our apartment, while not new, was clean and comfortable with a nice outdoor terrace. The pool area is well kept and the beach — private and naturist — is the real highlight. The on-site restaurant serves excellent fresh fish. The town is a taxi ride away and you really do need a car or bike to explore the area. But as a naturist escape, it delivers everything you need.

reviews.name: CoastalWalker
reviews.text: The location is stunning — right on the coast between Estepona and Marbella. The beach is naturist and peaceful. Gardens are well maintained and the pool area is inviting. The restaurant and bar are well run and serve decent food. The main downside is the lack of transport — a taxi or rental car is essentially essential. Some parts of the resort are showing their age. But the overall experience for naturists wanting direct beach access is hard to beat in Europe.

reviews.name: HonestNaturist
reviews.text: The site itself is beautiful — mature gardens, direct beach access, lovely pool — and the naturist community is friendly and respectful. However, the resort is starting to look tired. Several areas need painting and maintenance has slipped. Our apartment had dated fittings and the kitchen was basic. The restaurant is overpriced for what it is. That said, we had a pleasant enough week and the beach more than made up for the shortcomings.

reviews.name: FirstTimer2018
reviews.text: It helps to go in with realistic expectations. Costa Natura is not a hotel — it is a naturist apartment resort that has been here since 1976, and it shows. Apartments range enormously in quality; some have been modernised, others have not. Request a renovated unit. The site itself is lovely: right on the beach, good pool and jacuzzi, decent restaurant. The beach is darker with some pebble areas — but long, private, and genuinely naturist. A car is essential. Overall a good choice if you know what you are getting.
